title: Path around a school lawn
body: A school has a rectangular lawn that measures 30 m by 20 m. The school plans to lay a concrete path of uniform width all around the outside of the lawn, so that the lawn and the path together form a larger rectangle. The budget allows the lawn and the path together to cover exactly 816 m². The planning committee lets the width of the path be x metres. It wants to form a quadratic equation in x, solve it, and decide which root gives the actual width of the path.

title: A lamp post in a circular park
body: A circular park has a diameter of 25 m. Two gates, A and B, are at the two ends of a diameter on its boundary. The park committee wants to fix a lamp post P on the boundary so that the difference of its distances from the two gates is 17 m, with P nearer to gate B. Let BP = x m, so AP = (x + 17) m. Since AB is a diameter, angle APB = 90° (angle in a semicircle). The committee uses Pythagoras theorem to form a quadratic equation in x and checks its discriminant to decide whether such a point exists.
